The Sde Dov contamination crisis involves `widespread soil and groundwater pollution at the former Sde Dov airport and military base site in northern Tel Aviv`.[[1]](https://sdedov.co.il/%D7%96%D7%99%D7%94%D7%95%D7%9D-%D7%94%D7%A7%D7%A8%D7%A7%D7%A2%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%91%D7%A9%D7%93%D7%94-%D7%93%D7%91-%D7%94%D7%99%D7%9B%D7%9F-%D7%94%D7%AA%D7%92%D7%9C%D7%95-%D7%9E%D7%9E%D7%A6%D7%90/)[[2]](https://infospot.co.il/n/PFAS2)

### Key Details of the Contamination

- **Source of Pollution:** The contamination comes from **PFAS** (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, or "forever chemicals"), which accumulated over decades from the use of specialized firefighting foams for aviation fuel.[[1]](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/d9575fvxf)[[2]](https://infospot.co.il/n/PFAS2)[[3]](https://sdedov.co.il/%D7%96%D7%99%D7%94%D7%95%D7%9D-%D7%94%D7%A7%D7%A8%D7%A7%D7%A2%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%91%D7%A9%D7%93%D7%94-%D7%93%D7%91-%D7%94%D7%99%D7%9B%D7%9F-%D7%94%D7%AA%D7%92%D7%9C%D7%95-%D7%9E%D7%9E%D7%A6%D7%90/)
- **Discovery and Timeline:** 
	- The Water Authority warned the Ministry of Environmental Protection about PFAS in the Sde Dov area as early as 2022, with some groundwater wells showing levels up to 2,000% above permitted standards.
	- Because the ministry lacked a formal policy or testing requirement for PFAS at the time, the land was initially marketed and approved as clean.
	- Official announcements regarding widespread PFAS contamination across roughly a third of the Sde Dov district were made in **February 2026**.
	- Soil surveys released in **October 2026** (such as on plots developed by companies like Mivneh) showed extreme concentrations of chemicals like PFOS—reaching nearly 600 times direct-contact safety thresholds.[[1]](https://www.globes.co.il/news/article.aspx?did=1001534470)[[2]](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/d9575fvxf)[[3]](https://infospot.co.il/n/PFAS2)[[4]](https://www.calcalist.co.il/local_news/article/r1epofodzg)[[5]](https://www.gov.il/en/departments/topics/contaminated_land)[[6]](https://www.themarker.com/realestate/2026-10-14/ty-article/000001a1-39ab-d02c-adb9-79ff3aeb0000)
- **Impact on Construction and Municipal Works:** 
	- In **July 2026** , the Ministry of Environmental Protection ordered the Tel Aviv Municipality to halt infrastructure work after discovering that tens of thousands of tons of potentially contaminated soil had been excavated, piled, or moved across the site without proper documentation, separation, or safety supervision.
	- Courts and legal bodies (including the Herzliya Magistrates' Court) have paused lot-allocation drawings and delayed housing rights distributions for thousands of private landowners due to the legal and financial uncertainties surrounding cleanup.[[1]](https://www.calcalist.co.il/local_news/article/b1ypfnlvfe)[[2]](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/d9575fvxf)[[3]](https://www.ynet.co.il/economy/article/rjxns51100mx)
- **Legal and Market Fallout:** 
	- Apartment buyers and option holders have filed lawsuits against developers (such as Gindi Holdings) seeking to cancel transactions and recover funds, arguing that material information regarding toxic pollution was hidden or overlooked prior to marketing.
	- The contamination has raised broader alarms regarding other planned developments in Israel built on former airports or military sites, such as **Glilot**, **Herzliya Airport** , and the **Sirkin Base**.[[1]](https://www.ynet.co.il/economy/article/h1hombrrfg)[[2]](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/d9575fvxf)[[3]](https://www.globes.co.il/news/article.aspx?did=1001548834)[[4]](https://www.themarker.com/realestate/2026-07-08/ty-article/.highlight/0000019f-40c3-d07c-af9f-c8dfa5d10000)
